7599.name: Suvarnamukhi
7599.why: CWC carries the Suvarnamukhi on to the Arkavati and makes the Vrishabhavati its tributary. It is the other way round: the Suvarnamukhi joins the Vrishabhavati north of Kanakapura (Paani.Earth Vrishabhavathi and Arkavathi basin maps). Ended at the confluence.

7707.name: Vrishabhavati
7707.why: CWC starts the Vrishabhavati in Peenya, along the Nagarbhavi stream. The river rises at the Nandi Teertha temple by Sankey Tank in Malleshwaram (Paani.Earth; the district gazetteer and IISc also place the source in the old city) and meets the Nagarbhavi near Bangalore University: head redrawn from the OSM "Vrishabhavathi" ways. Below the Suvarnamukhi confluence it runs on to the Arkavati near Kanakapura, a stretch CWC gives to the Suvarnamukhi.

8607.name: Bava Malang
8607.why: CWC runs the Bava Malang on down the tidal creek to the Kasadi. From Taloja down, that creek is the Taloje (40450), which CWC lacks and which the Bava Malang joins at Taloja: the owner's correction, and OSM names the creek's water area "Taloje Creek" all the way from Taloja MIDC to the Kasadi. Ended at the confluence; above it CWC's line is the river's real course (within 60 m of OSM river way 777633651).

8809.name: Mithi
8809.why: CWC draws the Mithi (as "Mahim") from the hills a kilometre north of Vihar Lake. The river leaves the lake at the Vihar Lake Dam; course from the OpenStreetMap "Mithi River" waterway relation 6245575, dam to Mahim Creek.

16612.name: Mithari or Jojri
16612.why: Rises in the hills near Poondloo, Nagaur (the Jojari source on Wikipedia) and runs to the Luni east of Jodhpur. CWC stops the line about 5 km short and records it as inland drainage. Continued down the HydroRIVERS reaches to the Luni.

16613.name: Jojri
16613.why: The Jojari flows through Jodhpur, past Doli and Dhawa, and joins the Luni near Balotra (Mongabay, 2025; Wikipedia). CWC stops the line short and records it as inland drainage. Continued down the HydroRIVERS reaches to the Luni.

25543.name: Khan
25543.why: CWC runs the Khan (Kanh) up the western of Indore's two rivers, past Rajwada to Rau. That river is the Saraswati; the Kanh is the eastern one, from Limbodi lake through Musakhedi, and the two meet at Krishnapura, by Rajwada, below which the river is the Kanh (owner, 2026-10-06; Google Maps; OSM "Khan River"/"Kanh River"). Head redrawn from the OSM ways, from the lake's outlet to the confluence. The stretch it replaces is the Saraswati (40469 in data/added-rivers.json).

26630.name: Matla
26630.why: CWC cut the Matla in two where the Piyali joins and misspelt the upper 41 km, past Canning, "Malta". The two are one river (OSM "Matla" runs along both; Port Canning stands on the Matla): the upper half becomes the Matla's head, and 29679 is hidden as a river of its own.
